name: Ibuprofen
summary: A short-acting nonselective NSAID that balances analgesia, antipyresis, and anti-inflammatory effect with the classic COX-1/COX-2 tradeoff.
good: Short-term inflammatory pain, fever, and dysmenorrhea when a nonselective NSAID is appropriate.
bad: Active ulcer disease, advanced kidney disease, or patients already on multiple bleeding-risk drugs.
clinicalPearls: Short half-life means it wears off faster than naproxen, but the GI and renal warnings still apply.
mechanism: Reversible COX-1/COX-2 inhibition lowers prostaglandin synthesis, reducing pain, fever, and inflammation.
indications: Headache, fever, dysmenorrhea, sprains, dental pain, and short bursts of inflammatory pain.
interactionNotes: Anticoagulants, antiplatelets, ACE inhibitors, ARBs, and diuretics can turn a routine NSAID into a problem drug.

warnings: Ulcer disease, kidney disease, dehydration, late pregnancy, aspirin-sensitive asthma, and bleeding risk all matter.

Short half-life means it wears off faster than naproxen, but the GI and renal warnings still apply.
Nonselective, roughly balanced COX-1/COX-2 inhibition at typical doses.
Lower than many other nonselective NSAIDs at OTC doses, rising with dose and duration.
Present at higher doses/chronic use; can blunt aspirin’s antiplatelet effect if taken shortly before it (timing matters).
Reversible reduction in renal blood flow via COX-1-dependent prostaglandins — relevant in dehydration, CKD, or with ACE inhibitors/diuretics ("triple whammy").
